item.title: A generalized lasso formulation of weighted and regularized (nearly-)isotonic regression on graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.04018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study a regularized version of nearly-isotonic regression with respect to a general partial order. In this estimator the sum of squares is weighted, with some of the weights allowed to be zero, and an additional quadratic penalty is imposed. The only assumption we make is that the quadratic part of the objective function is strictly convex, and we show that this assumption is mild. First, we show that for all sufficiently large values of the penalty parameter the estimator coincides with the regularized isotonic regression, in which the penalty is replaced by the isotonic constraint. Further, we prove that the resulting problem can be written as a generalized lasso problem with a design matrix of full column rank and with the penalty matrix unchanged. Next, we derive the dual problem, which is a quadratic program with box constraints, and write it in a sparse form that can be solved by standard quadratic programming solvers for sparse problems.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Pastukhov

item.title: Nuisance structure and the detection boundary for population size: how profiling can change a rate, not only a constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.04453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A system contains an unknown number $N$ of units, each failing at an unknown common rate, each unit is removed once it fails. The failure-rate declines as units are removed, but after only a few failures the decline is too slight to distinguish from a constant rate, and the maximum-likelihood estimate of $N$ is infinite with substantial probability. This is a well-known feature of the model, but its probability has not been quantified. We show that about $N^{2/3}$ failures are needed before a finite population can be distinguished from an inexhaustible one, and that at this scale the profile log-likelihood ratio converges to that of a Gaussian shift experiment, in which an infinite estimate occurs with a calculable probability. The exponent is not a property of the model alone. Profiling annihilates the Taylor terms that the nuisance-parameters can reproduce, and detectability is governed by the first surviving term. For example, unknown drift in testing-effort reproduces the linear term, leaving a quadratic survivor and raising the requirement to $N^{4/5}$; in general the critical scale is $N^{2q/(2q+1)}$ for a survivor of order $q$. We obtain the limiting-law of the estimator, the null likelihood ratio distribution, and confidence sets that may be unbounded.
item.dc:creator: Yakir Berchenko

item.title: Statistical Theory in the Age of Machine-Assisted Mathematics
item.description: arXiv:2609.04481v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The computational revolution is advancing at an unprecedented pace. The combination of proof-assistant technologies and generative AI tools has recently enabled the solution of complex problems in pure mathematics at a scale that seemed unattainable only a few years ago, but they have not yet become standard tools in the development of statistical theory. In this paper we do not present new theoretical results; instead, we discuss five case studies involving classical problems in statistics and describe how a machine proof checker changes the thought process behind their proofs, in order to stimulate reflection on how these technologies may transform theoretical research and advanced statistical education. Statistical theory compresses mathematical content into expressions such as ``under the usual regularity conditions''; once AI writes the proofs and machines check them, the human reader is left with the statement and its hypotheses, which is exactly what such expressions compress. Against the fear that automation erodes skills, our experience was the opposite: what changes is the job of the theorist, which moves from the steps of a proof to its statement. The new paradigm can have positive effect also on methodologists and applied statisticians, because these tools allow for quick and precise check of formal guarantees necessary to justify the application of a specific model and/or methodology. We draw consequences for refereeing, doctoral teaching, and we encourage a collective effort toward shared formal libraries for statistics. Just as high-level programming languages revolutionized empirical research, machine-assisted formalization may introduce a new paradigm for the development, verification, and communication of statistical theory.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Coretto

item.title: Conformal-DP: A Density-Aware Mechanism for Differential Privacy over Riemannian Manifolds via Conformal Transformation
item.description: arXiv:2504.20941v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Differential Privacy (DP) is being increasingly adopted for non-Euclidean data that lie on complex, high-dimensional manifolds. Existing DP mechanisms for manifold data consider geometric properties when calibrating privacy perturbations, but they largely fail to capture variations in data density within datasets, leading to biased perturbations and suboptimal privacy-utility trade-offs due to heterogeneous data distributions. In this paper, we propose a novel density-aware differential privacy mechanism on Riemannian manifolds, referred to as Conformal-DP, that leverages conformal transformations to calibrate perturbations based on local densities and to induce a density-balanced geometry. We prove that our mechanism satisfies $\epsilon$-differential privacy on any complete Riemannian manifold under mild regularity assumptions. In addition, we derive a closed-form expected geodesic error bound that depends only on the underlying data density ratio and is independent of global curvature. Our empirical results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed Conformal-DP mechanism substantially improves the privacy-utility trade-off in heterogeneous data distribution settings, with worst-case performance comparable to state-of-the-art manifold DP mechanisms that assume uniformly distributed data.
item.dc:creator: Peilin He, Liou Tang, M. Amin Rahimian, James Joshi
